panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Color Doppler abdominal ultrasound of a school-aged child with hair-picking behavior showing a heterogeneous hyperechoic intragastric mass with no internal vascularity; the caption identifies this as the characteristic sonographic appearance of a gastric bezoar (gastric trichobezoar), a direct manifestation of the configured disease. [raw subtype: gastric trichobezoar] B: Grayscale abdominal ultrasound showing a markedly hyperechoic intraluminal interface (arrowheads) with prominent posterior acoustic shadowing (arrows), the textbook sonographic features of a gastric bezoar, directly attributed to gastric trichobezoar in the same school-aged patient; only the gastric component is shown, so no Rapunzel tail is claimed. [raw subtype: gastric trichobezoar]

panels.figure_caption: Abdominal ultrasonography of a gastric trichobezoar. A school-aged patient with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder was found to have a firm upper abdominal mass during a routine health examination. She reported early satiety but denied abdominal pain, vomiting, or weight loss. An abdominal examination revealed a well-defined, firm, non-tender mass measuring approximately 10 × 5 cm across the epigastrium, with a smooth surface and slight mobility on respiration. No hepatosplenomegaly or tenderness was noted, and the laboratory findings were unremarkable. Abdominal ultrasonography revealed a heterogeneous hyperechoic intragastric mass without internal vascularity on color Doppler imaging (A) and a markedly hyperechoic intraluminal interface (arrowheads) with prominent posterior acoustic shadowing (arrows) (B), which are considered sonographic features characteristic of a gastric bezoar. Upon further inquiry, her parents reported that she had exhibited hair-picking behavior approximately one year earlier, with a localized bald area noted at that time. In clinical practice, abdominal ultrasonography serves as an initial screening and clue-providing tool. Previous reports describe gastric trichobezoars on ultrasonography as well-defined intragastric hyperechoic masses with marked posterior acoustic attenuation or shadowing, sometimes initially mistaken for calcified lesions. In some cases, a characteristic a “hyperechoic ecoattenuating mass bordered by a trilinear wall” configuration has been noted. These lesions are most commonly located in the epigastric region corresponding to the stomach, although small bowel bezoars have also been reported [1,2,3]. The recognition of these characteristic patterns could prompt diagnostic confirmation via endoscopy and an assessment of the disease extent or complications based on computed tomography (CT), particularly in pediatric and young female patients with a palpable epigastric mass [4].

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT from a disease-focused article on Rapunzel syndrome in a child, showing a large intragastric mass with heterogeneous air-mixed density (arrowhead) that matches the caption's classic description of a gastric trichobezoar with mottled entrapped air bubbles; real patient image with no third-party restriction. [raw subtype: gastric trichobezoar] B: Axial contrast-enhanced CT from the same disease-focused Rapunzel syndrome case, showing the intragastric bezoar with mottled air-bubble density (arrowhead) filling the gastric body; the caption's specific manifestation plus the disease-focused article title support attribution to trichobezoar_rapunzel_syndrome; real patient image, no third-party restriction. [raw subtype: gastric trichobezoar]
panels.attribution_text: Wang and Weng. The Diagnostic Challenge of Rapunzel Syndrome: Multimodal Imaging Findings in a Child.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland) 2026. doi:10.3390/diagnostics16060940. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the gastric trichobezoar. The contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrates a large intragastric lesion with a heterogeneous, air-mixed density (arrowheads), consistent with bezoar formation, shown on coronal (A) and axial (B) images. Previous reports describe gastric trichobezoars on CT as well-defined intraluminal masses with a characteristic mottled appearance caused by numerous entrapped air bubbles within the tightly woven hairs. The lesion typically fills the gastric body and fundus and may extend beyond the pylorus into the duodenum or small bowel in Rapunzel syndrome or appear as separate small bowel masses [2,3,5,6]. Accordingly, abdominal CT is considered the single most effective modality for staging trichobezoars, enabling the assessment of the lesion extent, small bowel involvement, subsidiary bezoars, and obstruction or ischemic risk; evaluations of all are essential for surgical planning [3,7].

panels.rationale: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen in a real human patient from a case report of Rapunzel syndrome with secondary pancreatitis. The caption and in-text explicitly attribute the mottled intragastric mass and its extension into the duodenum to a trichobezoar in a patient with trichophagia, which is the defining manifestation of trichobezoar with Rapunzel syndrome. The visible gas-mottled gastric mass with duodenal extension matches the configured CT findings for this disease.
panels.attribution_text: Koushk Jalali et al. Laparoscopic Management of Acute Pancreatitis Secondary to Rapunzel Syndrome.. Case reports in surgery 2016. doi:10.1155/2016/7638504. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: CT image showing bezoar extension from stomach into duodenum.
in_text_mentions: plete blood count showed a mild leukocytosis of 11.6. Her Ranson criteria score on admission was 1 (mild pancreatitis). Her radiographic studies were performed including an abdominal X-ray, HIDA scan, and CT scan. The abdominal X-ray merely showed a paucity of gas. The CT scan of the abdomen however revealed a mass, which was considered as a possible trichobezoar in the stomach and proximal duodenum. This bezoar could strongly be related to the history of trichophagia and would be a cause of duodenal obstruction with secondary pancreatitis, which was detectable on CT imaging (Figures 1 and 2).

panels.rationale: Single-panel gross specimen photograph from a human patient (open-access case report of emergency laparotomy) showing a giant gastric trichobezoar with a long hair tail extending toward the small bowel — the defining gross manifestation of Rapunzel Syndrome. Caption explicitly names Rapunzel Syndrome and describes the hair tail extending through the pylorus into the proximal jejunum, so disease attribution is direct and specific. It is not a diagram, chart, control, animal, other-disease, or third-party image, and quality is clearly readable. The vocabulary key compact_hairball_specimen (gastric-cast hairball with elongated tail) matches exactly. No patient age or ethnicity is stated in the caption or in-text mentions for this panel, and no skin is shown. [raw subtype: Rapunzel syndrome with jejunal tail extension]

panels.rationale: Single-panel barium meal radiograph from a case report of trichobezoar presenting as Rapunzel syndrome. The image shows the stomach opacified with barium containing a large mottled, spongiform intraluminal filling defect, directly matching the captioned 'filling defect due to trichobezoar' and the in-text description of a barium-coated hairball seen as a mobile intraluminal filling defect. This is a real human-patient diagnostic image demonstrating the target disease, so it is included; the laterality ('LR') marker counts as an annotation.

in_text_mentions: and palpable mass in the epigastrium. The upper part of a large bezoar may be visible as a mass with a convex upper border projecting into the gastric air bubble. An erect abdominal radiograph and a supine radiograph may also show a prominent gastric outline with an intragastric mottled mass, outlined by gas in the distended stomach, mimicking a food-filled stomach. With a small amount of barium the hair-ball gets coated and becomes visible. Filling the stomach with barium demonstrates a mobile intraluminal filling defect of variable size, which may show extension into the duodenum [Figure 2].

in_text_mentions: owel obstruction, the radiologist suggested an abdominal computerized tomography (CT) scan with intravenous contrast. The CT scan revealed a significantly distended stomach, displacing surrounding structures, with a clearly demarcated intraluminal mass extending from the gastric cardia through the pylorus into the duodenum and proximal jejunal loops (Figure 1), with no signs of bowel wall ischemia. The mass was described as a banded, compact, bizarre, inhomogeneous formation with interposed air inclusions and no postcontrast enhancement. A diagnosis of Rapunzel syndrome was strongly suggested.

panels.rationale: Single AP chest/abdominal radiograph of a pediatric patient. The caption and in-text describe a large (≈15 × 7 cm) intragastric soft tissue mass with mottled lucencies displacing bowel loops, which is the classic plain-film appearance of a gastric trichobezoar. This is a real patient image with a disease-specific manifestation, so it is included and tagged to trichobezoar_rapunzel_syndrome; no small-bowel tail is demonstrated on this view, so no Rapunzel-extension subtype is assigned. Laterality marker 'L' counts as an annotation.

panels.figure_caption: This is an AP view X-ray of the chest and abdomen showing clear lung fields, a normal cardiac silhouette, and no bony deformity There is a well-defined intragastric soft tissue density mass is visible, projecting over the left upper quadrant and mid-abdomen with mottled lucencies, consistent with a trichobezoar. No evidence of perforation or bowel obstruction is observed.
in_text_mentions: egative. A large intragastric mass measuring approximately 15 × 7 cm was indicated by a radio-opaque mass inside the stomach that was displacing adjacent bowel loops inferiorly on an abdominal X-ray (Fig. 1). The results of the abdominal ultrasound showed no focal masses or abscesses, along with mild hepatomegaly and a uniform texture. Nonetheless, several enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes were observed, which most likely indicated inflammatory alterations. panels.rationale: Single-panel upper gastrointestinal endoscopy image from the case report 'Recurrent gastric trichobezoar in a child.' The caption and in-text explicitly state the endoscopy confirmed a recurrent gastric trichobezoar and that Figure 2 shows a small hair tail extending up to the duodenum (Rapunzel-syndrome pattern); the image visibly shows the dark, matted intragastric hair mass against gastric mucosa. Real human patient image, clear and substantial, no diagram, control, animal, or third-party issue. Age group 'child' is supported by the article title and the pediatric psychiatry referral; no ethnicity stated and no assessable skin, so those fields are null. [raw subtype: rapunzel_syndrome (gastric trichobezoar with duodenal hair tail)]

panels.figure_caption: Recurrent gastric trichobezoar confirmed by upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
in_text_mentions: been submitted to a laparotomy for removal of a large gastric trichobezoar. The upper gastrointestinal endoscopy confirmed the diagnosis of gastric trichobezoar. An anterior laparotomy was performed and a solid mass of hair of 12cm x 6cm x 4cm was removed. These dimensions were similar to those of the gastric trichobezoar removed 2 years earlier (Figure 1), in addition it presented a small tail of hair extending up to the duodenum (Figure 2). We referred the patient to a pediatric psychiatry consultation and so far she has had favorable progress without recurrent clinical or echographic signs.

Prior caption triage: keep. Age group remains unknown because only 'young female' is stated without a specific age; no ethnicity or skin is shown.

in_text_mentions: rning examination findings, computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast was obtained. Imaging demonstrated a large heterogeneous intraluminal gastric mass with a characteristic mottled appearance caused by entrapped air and debris, consistent with a gastric trichobezoar. The bezoar extended beyond the pylorus with an elongated tail into the jejunum, measuring approximately 40 cm, confirming Rapunzel syndrome, as illustrated in Figure 2. Associated findings included jejunojejunal intussusception, mild pancreatic ductal dilatation, and compression of the pancreatic head and neck.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Real contrast-enhanced axial CT from a human adolescent patient in a case report of a large gastric trichobezoar; the image shows a huge heterogeneous intraluminal gastric mass with internal gas mottling (spongiform hairball pattern) in a distended stomach, matching the configured disease. Caption explicitly states no pyloric extension, so this is gastric trichobezoar rather than Rapunzel syndrome. [raw subtype: gastric trichobezoar without small-bowel (Rapunzel) extension] b: Real contrast-enhanced coronal CT from the same human adolescent patient; shows the same huge heterogeneous intragastric mass with internal gas bubbles in a distended stomach, consistent with a gastric trichobezoar. Caption confirms no extension through the pyloric canal, excluding Rapunzel-type small-bowel tail. [raw subtype: gastric trichobezoar without small-bowel (Rapunzel) extension]

panels.rationale: Axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT from a case report explicitly titled 'Rapunzel Syndrome: A Case of Trichobezoar with Small Bowel Complications.' The caption identifies a heterogenous, mottled intraluminal gastric lesion outlined by oral contrast, which is the classic spongiform intragastric hairball appearance of a trichobezoar, and the in-text description confirms a large trichobezoar with small-bowel extension (Rapunzel syndrome). The asterisked gallbladder calculi are incidental and not a target-disease finding. Real untreated patient radiology image with clear disease attribution.

panels.rationale: Single-panel axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT from a real patient (Rapunzel Syndrome case report). It visibly shows a markedly distended stomach occupied by a mottled, spongiform intragastric hairball, the classic CT appearance of a trichobezoar. Caption directly attributes the finding to the bezoar; the red triangle marker indicates the mass. Gastric distension is additionally visible but absent from the vocabulary, so it is proposed. No small-bowel extension is shown in this panel, so no subtype is assigned. No ethnicity is stated.

Per rectal examination was normal. Lab results revealed a stable complete blood count, basic metabolic profile, liver function test values, normal bleeding time, and a normal coagulation profile. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen showed a distended stomach with the bezoar (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Axial contrast CT of the abdomen from a case report of Rapunzel Syndrome in a teenage girl. The caption and in-text describe dilated duodenal bowel loops with clumping of proximal jejunal loops and normal distal contrast flow, i.e., the partial small-bowel obstructive manifestation produced by the trichobezoar tail; the red arrowhead marks a mottled gas-containing rounded structure in the duodenal/proximal jejunal region consistent with the small-bowel hair tail. Attribution to trichobezoar_rapunzel_syndrome is supported by the disease-focused article title plus the captioned manifestation. The dilated/clumped loops themselves are not in the allowed vocabulary and are recorded as proposed findings.

panels.rationale: Single axial contrast CT of the abdomen from a case report of gastric trichobezoar causing small bowel obstruction. The caption and in-text explicitly attribute the dilated small bowel with mural stratification and inspissated material (arrow) to the trichobezoar case, and laparotomy confirmed a trichobezoar in the mid-jejunum, supporting the small-bowel hair-tail (Rapunzel) subtype of trichobezoar_rapunzel_syndrome. Real patient image, clear quality, disease-specific manifestation directly captioned. [raw subtype: small_bowel_hair_tail]

A CT of the abdomen exhibited dilated small bowel with mural stratification and inspissated material suggestive of moderate- to high-grade distal small bowel obstruction (Figure 4). The patient subsequently underwent uncomplicated midline laparotomy, resulting in the removal of a 13 × 3 cm trichobezoar from the mid-jejunum (Figure 5). in_text_mentions: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed a large trichobezoar extending from the stomach to the jejunum. The jejunal bezoar tail acts as a lead point for a long-segment small bowel-small bowel intussusception, resulting in telescoping of the small bowel and producing the characteristic "bowel-within-bowel" configuration. A second discontinuous small bowel-small bowel intussusception was identified within the midline lower abdomen extending to the right lower quadrant, suspected to be secondary to concreted stool and bezoar acting as a lead point (Figures 2, 3, 4).

in_text_mentions: The intraluminal masses were explored via gastric and jejunal enterotomies. A small longitudinal enterotomy was made proximal to the jejunal mass and it was milked retrograde and removed. Once removed, the mass appeared to be a trichobezoar. The gastric mass was milked retrograde from the pre-pyloric region and appeared similar to the trichobezoar from the jejunum. The stomach mass measured 10 x 4 x 4 cm, and the jejunal mass measured 5.8 x 3.5 x 2.2 cm, both consistent with trichobezoar on pathology exam (Figures 3-6).

The CT also revealed jejunojejunal intussusception with mesenteric lymphadenopathy serving as the probable lead point. There was no evidence of intestinal obstruction or pneumoperitoneum. Based on the imaging and clinical findings, surgical referral was advised for definitive management.

in_text_mentions: The contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) scan revealed an intraluminal mottled mass of mesh-like appearance occupying the entire stomach and extending beyond the second part of the duodenum, delineated by the oral contrast circumferentially, suggestive of a trichobezoar (Figure 1). The lack of any findings of biliary dilation or the presence of gallstones on the ultrasound further narrowed down the diagnosis.

Ultrasound may show an echogenic mass, but a CT scan is the diagnostic tool of choice since it provides a clear image of the bezoar delineated by the contrast dye, as seen in our case (Figure 1) [13]. Endoscopy also shows a large concretion of hair which is putrid and foul-smelling due to decomposition and fermentation of fats.

in_text_mentions: and trichophagia resulting in a possible trichobezoar. Initially, the patient denied to have ingested her hair, but after a thorough anamnesis, she admitted to have this habit, but rarely. The laboratory tests showed anemia (hemoglobin 8.7 g/dl, hematocrit 30.5%, and medium erythrocyte volume 67 fl). panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT of a human patient showing a large intraluminal mottled-gas mass extending from the stomach into the small bowel, consistent with a trichobezoar (Rapunzel syndrome). The mottled air-bubble pattern is a classic CT sign of a bezoar, and the small-bowel extension supports the Rapunzel subtype. No other disease is implicated. [raw subtype: Rapunzel syndrome (trichobezoar with small-bowel extension)]

in_text_mentions: A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen (Fig. 1) showed a large, clearly outlined intraluminal mass measuring 50.6 × 114.6 × 82.1 mm, stretching from the stomach into the duodenum and jejunum. The mass had a mottled gas pattern, a feature typical of bezoars. The jejunum demonstrated a transient intussusception with proximal bowel dilatation and the classic ‘target sign’, supporting the diagnosis of Rapunzel syndrome with jejunojejunal intussusception.

panels.rationale: Real upper-gastrointestinal endoscopic image from a human patient showing a giant intragastric trichobezoar: a compact, dark, matted hair mass filling the gastric lumen, visually matching the vocabulary finding of a compact/dark gastric hairball (synonyms: dark gastric trichobezoar, felted gastric hair mass, compacted hair meshwork). Disease attribution to trichobezoar_rapunzel_syndrome, subtype rapunzel_syndrome, is directly supported by the caption ('Endoscopic view of an intragastric trichobezoar'), the in-text description (giant trichobezoar extending from the distal esophagus and occluding the pylorus, with the mass extending into the first centimeters of the jejunum), and the article title ('Rapunzel syndrome: a rare presentation with giant gastric ulcer'). Prior caption triage also routed this figure to keep as a real patient image with no third-party restriction. The 'rare presentation' in the title refers to the associated giant gastric ulcer rather than the trichobezoar itself, so the endoscopic trichobezoar is a classic presentation. No skin is visible, and no age or ethnicity is stated in the caption or in-text. [raw subtype: rapunzel_syndrome]

in_text_mentions: its. On further evaluation, an ultrasound of the abdomen confirmed the presence of a large intragastric mass and an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan revealed a huge hypodense and heterogeneous gastric mass, appearing as a mesh, with multiple air bubbles seen within and surrounding the mass (Figure 1(a)). The mass filled the gastric fundus and duodenum and extended into the first centimeters of the jejunum. Finally, an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was performed and revealed the presence of a giant trichobezoar, extending from the distal esophagus and occluding the pylorus (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Single gross pathology photograph of a felted dark hair mass extracted from the bowel (jejunal enterotomy per in-text), pathologically confirmed as a trichobezoar. The small-bowel location beyond the gastric outlet in an adult matches Rapunzel syndrome, explicitly framed as atypical in the article title. Real patient specimen, clearly shows a target-disease manifestation, so it is included with high confidence. [raw subtype: rapunzel_syndrome_small_bowel_extension]
panels.attribution_text: Jacobson et al. Atypical Rapunzel Syndrome in an Adult Female: Trichobezoar Beyond the Gastric Outlet Leading to Gastrointestinal Perforation and Septic Shock.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.88436. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Gross pathology photograph showcases one of the bezoars that was extracted from the bowel.
in_text_mentions: The intraluminal masses were explored via gastric and jejunal enterotomies. A small longitudinal enterotomy was made proximal to the jejunal mass and it was milked retrograde and removed. Once removed, the mass appeared to be a trichobezoar. The gastric mass was milked retrograde from the pre-pyloric region and appeared similar to the trichobezoar from the jejunum. The stomach mass measured 10 x 4 x 4 cm, and the jejunal mass measured 5.8 x 3.5 x 2.2 cm, both consistent with trichobezoar on pathology exam (Figures 3-6).

panels.rationale: Real patient endoscopic image from a case report titled 'The rapunzel syndrome: an unusual trichobezoar presentation.' The caption and in-text explicitly describe a blackened voluminous hair mass (strands of hair, fibrin, food residue) in the stomach antrum/low body extending toward the pylorus and blocking the endoscope, with the case diagnosed as Rapunzel syndrome. The image visibly shows the matted intragastric trichobezoar, a direct clinical manifestation of the configured target disease. No third-party copyright, no other disease, not a diagram or control. Typicality is atypical per the article title emphasizing an unusual presentation. No ethnicity or age stated for this figure; endoscope overlay text (F07/AVE/1/60/NHSC) is camera metadata, not a clinical annotation.

panels.figure_caption: Endoscopic image of a trichobezoar extending into the pylorus.
in_text_mentions: gestive tract was performed as part of the preoperative work-up, findings revealing a blackened, voluminous mass composed of strands of hair, fibrin and food residue in the stomach, located in the antrum and low body, extending towards the pylorus and blocking passage of the endoscope (Figures 1 and 2). A computed tomography scan of the abdomen was also performed and, in addition to identifying a hypodense intragastric mass, results showed hypodense circular areas in the small bowel and the presence of bowel intussusception (Figures 3 and 4), findings compatible with the Rapunzel syndrome [7].

panels.rationale: Single coronal non-contrast CT panel showing a small bezoar in the mid/lower abdomen indicated by a red arrow. Disease attribution is strongly supported by the disease-focused article title ('Atypical Rapunzel Syndrome...Trichobezoar Beyond the Gastric Outlet') and the explicit caption/in-text identification of a bezoar. The in-text specifically mentions small bowel involvement, and the arrow points to the lower abdomen consistent with a small-bowel tail of the trichobezoar (Rapunzel syndrome). The article title confirms an adult female patient.

panels.figure_caption: Non-contrast CT scan, coronal view, displaying a small bezoar seen in the mid abdomen (red arrow).
in_text_mentions: therwise afebrile and non-tachycardic. On exam, the patient appeared uncomfortable with dry mucous membranes as well as abdominal distension and rebound tenderness consistent with peritonitis. Significant labs at the time included hyponatremia, an elevated anion gap, acute kidney injury, and iron deficiency anemia. No leukocytosis or elevated lactate was seen (Table 1). On a non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan, there appeared to be a poorly defined, heterogeneous, low to intermediate attenuated mass within the gastric body and small bowel which raised concern for a bezoar (Figure 1, 2).
